before: If system utilisation increases → subscription cost per operational unit decreases.
after: For a fixed subscription fee over a defined period, higher completed volume reduces the fixed subscription cost per unit. A constant usage-based charge per unit does not decrease merely because volume rises.

before: Recurring subscription fees accumulate to exceed capital ownership cost in long-term deployments without fee renegotiation.
after: Recurring subscription fees may exceed capital ownership cost, depending on purchase prices, subscription and service fees, usage charges, and the comparison horizon.

before: Capital purchase imposes high upfront exposure but lower lifetime cost under stable multi-year contracts. RaaS reduces initial risk but accumulates to exceed ownership cost if client contracts remain stable for 4+ years.
after: Capital purchase imposes upfront investment. Compare its installed and ongoing costs with the RaaS initial and recurring costs over the same horizon. Without prices, fees and operating assumptions, neither a lower lifetime cost nor a crossover year can be calculated.

before: Capital purchase creates higher upfront exposure but lower lifetime cost if the system remains deployed long-term.
after: Capital purchase creates upfront exposure; whether its lifetime cost is lower depends on the two cost paths over a common horizon.

before: Lower if system remains deployed · service fees continue
after: Compare installed and recurring costs over the same horizon

before: Can exceed ownership cost in long-term deployments
after: May exceed ownership cost, depending on fees and horizon

before: Determines how efficiently automation capacity is used. If utilisation declines, effective cost per operational unit rises regardless of pricing model.
after: For a fixed cost component over a defined period, lower completed volume raises that component’s cost per unit. A constant usage-based per-unit charge is unchanged by volume alone.
